objective: Distinguish the Bible Quiz V4 learner submission from its explanation in every completed answer review without changing existing daily selection, scoring, reward ledger, or runtime.
productionBaselineEvidence: Based on verified Android 1.3.2 staging candidate fix/conso-144-dark-staging-20261116 SHA 9221909b98f8faac5930711be6297e52fb2ec8d1. Main/production and live backend remain unchanged by this PR.
chosenApproach: Add a read-only, owner-scoped optional RPC for previously submitted answers; render submitted answer, rationale, and accepted answers under distinct labels. Keep the old RPC and grader untouched.
selectionRationale: The screenshot displays r.rationale instead of the answer. Changing scoring without the user's original submission is not evidence-based. An additive endpoint avoids reverting post-V4 selection hotfixes.
preserveBehaviors: Only authenticated attempt owner can read their own saved answers after submitting.
No correct keys or submitted answers for started attempts.
One daily Bible Quiz attempt; same questions and existing grading algorithm.
No modification to BP ledger, QMP/finance, native runtime, production or Play Store.
Existing web/Android clients continue functioning without the optional endpoint.
acceptanceChecks: Run scoped structural and security review tests.
Verify API returns only user's submitted answers for completed/pending attempts and returns no review while started.
Confirm cross-user attempt_id cannot retrieve the submission.
Review question, actual answer, rationale and accepted aliases display correctly.
Confirm no change to existing scoring/daily question-selection RPC and no mutation to production.
Staging-only Android JS bundle export passes for exact candidate SHA, without deploying or requiring an Expo token.
releaseStatus: DEV PR only; additive SQL migration not applied; no OTA or web publication.

alternativeApproaches: Modify the existing V4 get/grade function: rejected because newer anti-repeat changes could be rolled back and scoring evidence is missing.
Store submissions solely in the browser: rejected because refresh and multi-device review would be incomplete.
